samples.question: This picture shows a network drawn on a white page. Every disc is a junction and every straight gray bar is a link joining the two junctions at its ends. Bars meet only at junctions, no bar crosses another bar, and no bar passes through a junction that is not one of its two ends. The whole network hangs together, and it contains exactly one closed loop: exactly one ring of junctions can be walked all the way round and back to its starting junction without using any bar twice. Every other part of the network is a branch that eventually dead-ends, so leaving the loop means you can never get back without retracing a bar. Three junctions are coloured, one blue, one orange and one purple, and every other junction is dark grey. Exactly one of the three coloured junctions lies on the closed loop. How central a junction looks, how many bars touch it, and where it sits on the page do not matter; only whether you can walk round the loop through it counts. Which coloured junction lies on the closed loop? Answer blue, orange, or purple.
